scope: Focused static teardown-lifetime audit of platform remove, panel notifier callback dispatch/unregister, report workqueue admission, IRQ/event buffer, and open cdev/input mappings.

stock_function_revalidation.meaning: AArch64 instructions, relocations, section and symbol sizes matched for all six pairs; this does not settle external notifier lifetime.

teardown_order: syna_dev_remove calls syna_cdev_quiesce, then panel_event_notifier_unregister(cookie) when active_panel and cookie are present.
The remove path continues with sysfs/helper-workqueue cleanup, cdev retirement, syna_dev_disconnect (including managed IRQ/workqueue teardown), and object cleanup.

The registered panel callback can call change_tp_state, which touches the global tpd_cdev state lock and report-workqueue slot. The cdev quiesce gate does not serialize the external notifier callback.
The reconstructed notifier unregister has no in-flight callback drain, so a callback copied by trigger before unregister can begin after unregister returns and overlap later TPD teardown.

finding.confidence: HIGH for callback-after-unregister window; runtime manifestation not exercised
mechanism: Stock panel_event_notification_trigger locks its registry, copies callback/client_data, unlocks, performs the KCFI type check, then invokes the copied callback indirectly.
Stock panel_event_notifier_unregister locks the registry, zeros the slot fields, unlocks, and returns; it does not wait for a callback already copied by trigger.
Therefore unregister prevents later registry lookups but does not guarantee that no callback is executing or about to enter the TPD module when remove proceeds.
finding.impact: Possible callback use of TPD global state or workqueue during/after teardown; exact fault depends on callback timing and the concurrent device/module teardown path.
finding.source_change: None in this commit. A TPD-only entry counter cannot close the interval between dispatcher copying the function pointer and entering the callback.

binary_observations.unregister_behavior: takes registry mutex, clears callback/client/panel/tag fields, unlocks and returns; no wait/completion/refcount synchronization is present

docker_provider_caveat.provider_behavior: The Docker source has a separate implementation with the same API names that calls callbacks while holding panel_client_mutex; unregister serializes on that mutex. This behavior must not be attributed to the stock external panel_event_notifier.ko.
docker_provider_caveat.abi_note: The Docker header places panel at offset 8 and early_trigger at offset 24; stock notifier assembly reads panel at offset 16, while the stock TPD callback reads early_trigger at offset 12. Do not build a replacement against this header without resolving the legacy binary layout.

recommended_fix_boundary.owner: the actual panel_event_notifier provider/API, or a provider-independent callback lifetime mechanism with a non-unloadable trampoline
recommended_fix_boundary.required_contract: Unregister must prevent new dispatch and wait for callbacks previously selected by trigger. A per-registration in-flight count must be incremented while holding the same registry lock used to select the callback; unregister marks the registration retiring under that lock and waits for the count to reach zero.
recommended_fix_boundary.integration_gate: Preserve the stock callback ABI/KCFI and notification offsets; identify whether the shipped provider is the external stock module or the Docker built-in compatibility provider before changing code.
validation_needed: canonical Docker build against the intended export surface
trigger/unregister concurrency stress with KASAN/lockdep or a deterministic race harness
runtime module unload and NX809J panel-event teardown

limitations: Static binary/source review only; no race was run on hardware.
The current Docker compatibility provider and its header are not proven to be the target runtime provider.
This audit documents a lifecycle risk and does not declare zte_tpd teardown safe.
